# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration 1
**Intent**: Create initial capability from scratch.
- Added `prompt.md` with strict "Literal Values ONLY" contract, a 6-step Operational Procedure to prevent skipped verification, and "No Error Strings" rule.
- Added `task_template.md` reinforcing the literal values and targeted modification constraints.
- Targets failure clusters: Formulas (KNOWLEDGE), Empty cells (BEHAVIORAL), Error strings (KNOWLEDGE), and general Value Mismatches.
- Safe because these are additive constraints that passing tasks already satisfy.

- Changes I made:

    - prompt.md: Restructured "Operational Procedure" to include a mandatory "Verify & Audit" step with a checklist for literal values, precision, minimal mutation, and coverage.
    - task_template.md: Strengthened the finish condition to include type accuracy and minimal mutation checks.
- Expected effect:
    - Fix Type Mismatches (416-15, 80-42) by ensuring correct Python types are written.
    - Fix Over-Mutation (227-40, 395-36) by making the mutation check a mandatory step.
    - Fix Missing Outputs (9569, 37456) by encouraging better verification of the final range.
- Building on prior RESULTS: Used cand_0001 result to identify that "Literal Values" and "Minimal Mutation" rules were known but skipped. Switched from "advice" to "audit checklist" structure.
- Refuted hypotheses: None.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: Complex computation errors (51-12, 39046) may need worked examples if this iteration doesn't move them.
- Focus next iteration: If computation errors persist, introduce worked examples for complex row-by-row logic.

## Iteration cand_0003 — Fix Infinite Loops and Logic Failures via Reflection and Sample Tracing
- Changes I made:
    - prompt.md: Added "Failure Reflection" to Recovery Guidance to stop infinite loops.
    - prompt.md: Added a mandatory "Sample Trace" step to the "Compute" phase of the Operational Procedure.
- Expected effect:
    - Fix Infinite Loops (51-12, 267-18, 227-40, 2768, 9726) by forcing the agent to analyze failure root causes instead of repeating code.
    - Fix Logic & Coverage failures (560-12, 39046, 50768, 37456, 43436) by ensuring computation logic is verified on sample rows before full application.
- Building on prior RESULTS:
    - Used cand_0002 results to identify that the "Audit Checklist" was good but didn't prevent logic errors or infinite loops during the "Compute" phase.
- Refuted hypotheses: None.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: Some complex computations might still fail if the logic is fundamentally misunderstood; if these persist, I'll try worked examples of common spreadsheet idioms.
- Focus next iteration: If logic errors persist, introduce worked examples for row-by-row conditional summation or complex filtering.
